blocks.text: The review opened on {{fact:f:E-2019-001.start}}. We owe the client one recommendation per patent family: keep it, extend it, or let it lapse. Each recommendation rests on the record and states what would change it.
The client contact is Gary Smith, General Manager. He reads the conclusion first. Every family summary opens with its recommendation.

items: Docket reconciliation. Sharon Woods compares the client's docket with USPTO and foreign office records. Every open date goes on our docket as a reminder. We act on a date only on the client's written instruction.
Chain of title. Amanda Schwartz checks the recorded assignments for each family. She also reads the inventors' assignment and employment agreements. Gaps go on her issues list with a proposed fix.
Prosecution and claims. I take the families in order of nearest deadline. For each one I record status, remaining term, payment dates, and claim scope.
Product mapping. Amanda Schwartz maps the claims to the product information Gary Smith sends. Where his description is thin, we ask him. We do not fill the gap ourselves.
Recommendation and report. Heather Munoz reviews each family summary and sets the recommendation. She signs the report. Legal conclusions are hers.

blocks.text: This is a review. It does not include new filings, office action responses, or validity and infringement opinions.
Some families will look like continuation candidates. Take those to Heather Munoz with a rough cost first. The client hears the cost in the same message as the suggestion.

items: Client contact goes through me. Heather Munoz approves anything that carries a recommendation before it goes out.
One issues list per family, kept in the matter folder. Close an issue only with a note of how it closed.
Record time to the matter as usual. The fee is fixed, but we need to know what the review costs us.
Mark every family summary privileged and confidential. The client may circulate the report internally, so draft for that reader.
The client's docket may not match office records. Treat the office records as correct until shown otherwise.
Some inventors may have left the company. Their agreements decide whether title can be fixed without new signatures.
Product information may lag the claims work. Map only against descriptions the client has confirmed as current.
Scope drift. Whether a product is clear to sell is a freedom-to-operate question. It goes to Heather Munoz, not into the review.

blocks.text: Before the End of Next Week

items: Today: I send Gary Smith the document request. It covers the docket export, file copies, inventor agreements, and the current product list.
Sharon Woods opens the matter on our docket and starts the reconciliation as the export arrives.
Amanda Schwartz pulls the USPTO assignment records for every family and opens the issues list.
I set up the family index in the matter folder. One row per family. One owner per row.
Team check-in each Monday, fifteen minutes, until the reconciliation closes.

blocks.text: Anything that touches a deadline comes to Sharon Woods and me the same day. Everything else waits for Monday.
